records.conditionSummary: Only when lexical and semantic signals are complementary; if both return the same passages or one is poorly tuned, merging adds latency without much gain.
records.mustConvey: complementary retrievers / otherwise only adds latency
records.bindingReason: When the retrievers overlap or one is poorly tuned, 'hybrid improves recall' is false.
records.notes: g2 takeaway ('merges ... to maximize recall'), g1 takeaway ('a hybrid approach is likely best'), u2_a1 ('would be beneficial') and u7_n2 ('expands the scope of results') state the benefit unconditionally. g6 takeaway / u7_n7 say each step has 'specific conditions' but not this one, so u7_n2 is not 'frame'. Including g1/u2_a1 as claim cards is a judgement call (they are generator inferences of the same claim).

records.claimSummary: The fused candidate list is built from each retriever's top 50.
records.conditionSummary: At most 100 candidates, usually fewer due to overlap.
records.bindingReason: Without the bound the candidate count (and so the reranking cost) is misstated.

records.claimSummary: A cross-encoder reranker rescores passages, judging relevance far more accurately.
records.conditionSummary: Because it is expensive, it runs only on the fused candidates, never on the whole collection.
records.mustConvey: only on fused candidates, not the whole collection
records.bindingReason: Read as scoring the whole collection, the description of the reranker would be false.

records.claimSummary: Reranking improves the precision of the top results.
records.conditionSummary: It does not guarantee that the final answer is correct.
records.mustConvey: does not guarantee a correct answer
records.bindingReason: The precision claim stays true; the caveat warns against over-reading it.
records.notes: g3 and u4_ax1 speak of limits ('limited by initial retrieval', 'constrained by ... quality of initial retrieval') but not of the final answer's correctness; judged not to carry this specific caveat. u7_n4 sits in g6 whose takeaway says no step guarantees correctness.

records.claimSummary: Reranking improves top-result precision / judges relevance more accurately.
records.conditionSummary: It can only reorder what retrieval found; if the right passage is not among the candidates, reranking cannot recover it.
records.mustConvey: can only reorder retrieved candidates; cannot recover a missed passage
records.bindingReason: When the right passage was not retrieved, reranking does not improve the results, so the claim is misleading in that case.
records.notes: u7_n4 'organizes the retrieved results' conveys the bound only implicitly (medium-low). u4_ax3 'cannot compensate for poor initial retrieval' also carries it.

records.claimSummary: The cross-encoder judges relevance far more accurately than either retriever.
records.conditionSummary: A passage can be highly relevant yet out of date, which no relevance score detects.
records.mustConvey: relevant but out of date is not detected
records.bindingReason: Relevance accuracy stays true; staleness is a separate limitation.

records.claimSummary: The language model answers only from the top 8 passages, citing them.
records.conditionSummary: If none of the passages addresses the question, it should say so rather than answer from general knowledge.
records.mustConvey: if no passage addresses the question, say so
records.bindingReason: The instruction to answer only from the passages stays true; the exception adds the decline path.
records.notes: u5_n4 has no arrows; the shape u5_n3 'Check Passage Relevance' is too vague to carry it. Binding could be argued 'claim' (g4 'answers questions from provided passages' is misleading when none are relevant).

records.claimSummary: Citations let a reader check each claim against its passage.
records.conditionSummary: They do not show whether the passage itself is current.
records.mustConvey: citations do not show currency / freshness
records.bindingReason: Citations still allow checking claims; the currency gap is a caveat.

records.claimSummary: Measured relevance/latency/cost per configuration (e.g. hybrid + reranker 88%, 190 ms, $0.95).
records.conditionSummary: Figures come from one collection and one 400-question query set; fewer exact identifiers may mean a smaller BM25 gain, and a different reranker has different latency.
records.mustConvey: one collection and one query set; may differ elsewhere
records.bindingReason: Taken as general figures they are misleading for another collection or reranker.
records.notes: u6_n1 mentions the 400-question internal test set but not the single-collection limit; u6_n5 carries it but has no arrow. Binding claim vs set is debatable: the numbers are true as measurements.

records.claimSummary: Teams with a strict latency budget can rerank fewer candidates (e.g. top 30).
records.bindingReason: The option still exists; the recall cost is its price.

records.claimSummary: Vector retrieval alone missed the correct passage for 31 of 50 queries.
records.conditionSummary: Only for queries consisting mainly of an error code.
records.bindingReason: Read as 31/50 of all queries, the figure would be false.

records.claimSummary: Embeddings must be recomputed, taking about 6 hours for this collection.
records.bindingReason: Without the trigger it reads as a recurring 6-hour cost, which is false.

notes: Examples (u8, u9 quoted strings, u13, u37), definitions (u4-u5, u10, u20-u21) and the k-parameter elaboration (u22) are not recorded. u25 (kept 50 rather than 100) is a design rationale, not a limiting condition. The generator's analysis nodes (*_a1, *_ax*) and frame takeaways were treated as normal readable nodes; several state the hybrid benefit unconditionally. Group-to-group arrows (g0->g1 ...) were not used as links between cards.
